items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1958-11-14
items.q: Dick and I were invited over.

ctx.x: Well, the first time I heard Bunk was in his twenties. That's the first time I heard Bunk when Bunk was a younger man. I heard Bunk in New Orleans too. I heard Bunk here on Parades. I heard Bunk at Banquets. You know, we called Bunk kids. We called them Bunk kids at the Hopes Hall. I heard him at the – they never gave too many at the Economy Hall. But the Perseverance Hall and the New Hall there and also the – where the big I-Lewy used to stay at Artesian Hall. That's where the Bunk was mostly.

Tell a little bit more about those Bunk kids. They had one at the Union when you were up in Chicago the last time. Dick and I were invited over. But of course there they lined up, you know, and went around and got chicken. It wasn't served to them or anything. But were the old Bunk kids more formal? How did they – what did they do? Have music or what all did they do?

Well, I'll tell you how they did. The organizations would have, say like it would be the anniversary of the society. It would be two years old probably next – this year or three or whatever year, you know – well every year on that date they would have this banquet. Well they'd take – so many members would be of the Catholic faiths, so many would be of the Baptist faiths. But one year they'd go to a Baptist church if it was a Baptist, well they'd go on a Sunday evening, you know, for this service. If it was a…
